participants.role: instrument maintenance and calibration research team

goals.label: Complete a four-slot survey batch by the first dusk
Complete a four-slot calibration batch without promising unusable capacity
Complete a four-slot follow-up batch by the first dusk

opportunities.label: Negotiate the first allocation while the maintenance team alone has current hardware evidence.
Recheck instrument condition after the scheduled maintenance interval.
Compare the teams' completed work, broken promises and cumulative allocation equity.
Reconsider a prior promise using the event-grounded counterfactual retry.

debrief.objective: Practice coordinating scarce shared capacity under private condition information and real deadlines. Distinguish nominal capacity, supported evidence, endorsed promises and completed research. This is a fictional decision practice task; skill transfer is unvalidated.
questions: Who knew the hardware condition before the first allocation, and what caused it to become available to others?
Which promises fit actual usable capacity at settlement, and which failed? Cite the events.
Which team carried the opportunity cost of your allocation, and what happened over repeated rounds?
Would an inspection have changed the information available before your decision, after accounting for its finite credit cost?

transfer.prompt: A new laboratory advertises twelve instrument slots. Three teams need four slots each, but only the engineer has a fresh reliability report. Which plan best manages the uncertainty?
options: Promise four slots to all three teams immediately because twelve slots are advertised.
Ask for the dated report or buy a fresh check, disclose its limits, and make a feasible allocation with an explicit review point.
Allocate everything to the most confident team and record its confidence as direct evidence.
transfer.rationale: A nominal resource limit is not verified usable capacity. Legitimate evidence, an explicit cost-aware allocation and a later review point make the promise testable. This answer is conceptual and does not establish learning transfer.

sources.title: Project-authored shared-instrument allocation experiment; not an operational observatory or validated training curriculum.
